title: Pricing Inflation Swaps in the Japanese Bond Market - San Francisco Fed
gist: SF Fed finds Japanese inflation swap and JGBi breakeven rates are nearly identical, a puzzle versus the US where TIPS liquidity premiums create a wedge, and a model predicts large premiums that don't show up.

insights.claim: Japanese 10-year inflation swap rates and inflation-indexed JGB breakeven rates are nearly identical, unlike the US where swap rates sit systematically above TIPS breakevens.
insights.speaker: Jens Christensen
insights.so_what: Japanese BEIs may be cleaner inflation signals than expected, or other forces are at work.
insights.quote: Japanese inflation swap rates (green line) and inflation-indexed JGB BEI rates (blue line) are nearly identical.

insights.claim: Inflation-indexed JGBs are only about 1% of Japanese government debt, implying large liquidity premiums, and they offer deflation protection that should push breakevens up.
insights.speaker: Jens Christensen
insights.so_what: Two offsetting premiums should distort Japanese BEIs.
insights.locator: Inflation swaps and BEI rates in the United States and Japan

insights.claim: The estimated total bond-specific premium was large and negative until about 2022 and positive afterwards, implying a swap-BEI spread that is not observed in the data.
insights.speaker: Jens Christensen
insights.so_what: Model-implied wedge is unexplained; some other force is pricing Japanese inflation swaps.

insights.claim: The value of deflation protection in inflation-indexed JGBs was around a full percentage point for extended periods but has dropped to near zero since inflation firmed after 2022.
insights.speaker: Jens Christensen
insights.so_what: Deflation optionality is no longer priced into Japanese linkers.

insights.claim: Dealers' need to hedge in the inflation-indexed JGB market may explain swap pricing, but the implied distortions averaging 0.24% with a 0.85% standard deviation are too large to explain it alone.
insights.speaker: Jens Christensen

insights.claim: Reading expected Japanese inflation from JGBi breakeven rates likely requires adjusting them for the embedded liquidity and deflation-protection premiums.
insights.speaker: Jens Christensen
insights.so_what: Raw Japanese BEIs are a noisy gauge of inflation expectations relevant to BOJ policy and JGB trades.
